summary: @yeaft/webchat-agent exposes host shell and filesystem to a remote WebSocket peer
details: The agent, launched via the yeaft-agent CLI or installed as a systemd/launchd/Windows service, opens an outbound WebSocket to a configurable coordination server and treats messages from that peer as commands. A 'terminal_create' message causes the agent to spawn a PTY running the host's default shell (process.env.SHELL || bash on Unix, PowerShell/cmd on Windows) via pty.spawn, and subsequent 'terminal_input' messages are written raw into that PTY (term.pty.write(msg.data)). Additional message handlers (read_file, write_file, git_*, upgrade_agent, restart_agent) give the same remote peer arbitrary file read/write, git operations, and agent self-update on the installer's host. Whoever controls the configured server has interactive shell access and full-file access to any machine running the agent. service/linux.js also prepends ~/.local/bin and ~/.npm-global/bin to PATH in the generated systemd unit, making the agent's shell environment PATH-mutable by any writer to those directories.
